Maladaptive Strategies.value: mentally rehearse worst case scenarios to feel prepared
Seeing other people that were involved in the event or that look similar
constantly monitor own thoughts for signs of going crazy

Threat.value: I frequently look behind me to check if someone is following me
I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked

Memory.value: Sometimes I feel the full emotional intensity of the event without any clear image or memory
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns

Negative Appraisals.value: I have lost my connection to my community and culture
The event happened because of the way I acted
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore

issues.explanation: The negative appraisals are not well matched to the trauma type and profile. After a mugging/robbery, self-blame is plausible, but 'Lost Community' and especially 'Lost Meaning' suggest broader identity/existential disruption that is hard to reconcile with the otherwise threat-focused robbery profile unless there is additional context not represented elsewhere.

Within the Memory node, 'Vivid Memory' and 'Emotion Without Image' pull in opposite directions: one implies clear, detailed recollection, while the other implies intense affect without clear recall. These can both occur in PTSD, but selecting both as core memory characteristics without any qualifier makes the node clinically inconsistent.

'Thought Monitoring: constantly monitor own thoughts for signs of going crazy' is a poor fit with the rest of the profile. The threat items are focused on external physical danger after a mugging, whereas this strategy targets fear of mental disintegration/panic not otherwise represented in Threat, Memory, or Appraisals. It does not align well with the formulation either, because Maladaptive Strategies is strongly linked to Threat and Memory, but the selected strategy addresses a different symptom theme.

The negative appraisals are not well aligned with the trauma type and the rest of the profile. For a single-incident mugging/robbery, 'Lost Community' and especially the global nihilistic appraisal 'Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore' are hard to reconcile with the otherwise circumscribed threat/checking profile unless there is broader contextual trauma not represented here.

Within the Memory node, 'Emotion Without Image' and 'Vivid Memory' pull in opposite directions as dominant descriptions of trauma recall. They can occasionally coexist, but selecting both as defining memory items for this profile creates a clinically questionable mix without other items clarifying fragmented versus vivid re-experiencing.

The negative appraisal profile is not well aligned with the trauma type and the rest of the formulation. For a single mugging/robbery, 'Lost Community: I have lost my connection to my community and culture' is hard to connect to the other selected items; there are no accompanying trigger, threat, memory, or strategy items about community, cultural shame, social rejection, or identity-based trauma. It reads as a different problem theme from the rest of the profile.

Within Negative Appraisals, 'Lost Meaning: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore' is unusually global and severe relative to the rest of the selected items, which otherwise center on fear, vigilance, and self-blame after a mugging. Without broader hopelessness, depression-linked, or pervasive defeat themes elsewhere in the five components, this item feels clinically disconnected.
